The ish pashut sustains himself from the bechina of pre-Torah world-sustenance (the same domain as Package 1). The tzaddik in his state of peshitut draws from the Ten Utterances-dimension of creation. The ish pashut is therefore the human embodiment of the pre-Torah stratum — same essential nature as the package.
additions.source_quote: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁמְּבַטְּלִין מֵהַתּוֹרָה, הוּא בְּחִינַת אִישׁ פָּשׁוּט מַמָּשׁ

additions.reason: The pre-Torah world was sustained 'by His chesed alone' (בְּחַסְדּוֹ לְבַד). The text equates this with 'chesed chinam' — free, unconditional lovingkindness — and explicitly calls it a bechina of the pre-Torah sustenance. The Torah quotes the verse 'כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ' as the scriptural expression of this quality. Chesed chinam and matnat chinam are near-synonyms in the text, but chesed chinam emphasizes the quality of divine grace rather than the metaphor of a treasury. Both belong to the same Package 1 domain.
additions.source_quote: קֹדֶם קַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה הָיָה הָעוֹלָם מִתְקַיֵּם רַק בְּחַסְדּוֹ... וְהָיָה עִקָּר קִיּוּם הָעוֹלָם עַל־יְדֵי חַסְדּוֹ לְבַד

additions.reason: The text explicitly defines 'derech eretz' as a bechina of the Ten Utterances embedded in worldly conduct: 'עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת שֶׁהֵם מְלֻבָּשִׁין בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ.' The text equates derech eretz with the path to Eretz Yisrael, making it part of the same conceptual cluster.
additions.source_quote: נִמְצָא שֶׁעֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת שֶׁהֵם מְלֻבָּשִׁין בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, הַיְנוּ בְּיִשּׁוּב הָעוֹלָם... הֵם דֶּרֶךְ לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל

additions.reason: Yishuv ha-olam (civilized conduct / settlement of the world) is the concrete expression of the Ten Utterances in the world. The text says that pre-Torah existence consisted of 'עֲשִׂיַּת הָעוֹלָם' and 'דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ' — worldly conduct — and that this is the domain of the Ten Utterances in which the Torah lies hidden. Yishuv ha-olam is therefore a bechina of the Ten Utterances domain.

additions.reason: The text states that 'all the Torah is contained in the Ten Commandments, and the Ten Commandments before the giving of the Torah were hidden inside the Ten Utterances of Creation.' This makes the Ten Commandments a bechina of the Ten Utterances — they share the same essential structure (both are 'ten,' both carry the full Torah). They belong to the same package as a bechina-equivalent of עשרה מאמרות.
additions.source_quote: כִּי כָל הַתּוֹרָה כְּלוּלָה בַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת, וְאָז קֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הָיוּ הָעֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת נֶעְלָמִין בַּעֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶם נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם

additions.reason: The true tzaddik is described as the 'great ish pashut' who draws from the pre-Torah dimension and thereby gives life to all the simple people below him. He is the living conduit of the Package 1 reality — the one who accesses matnat chinam and the Ten Utterances dimension in his moments of peshitut. He belongs in Package 1 as the personal embodiment of this entire domain.
